style.vernacular: Small highland capital at about 1,600 m under the Maloti foothills: low 1-3 storey buildings along the paved Kingsway axis, local honey-coloured sandstone on colonial-era civic and church buildings, cream and ochre painted render on newer blocks, face-brick and plain concrete in the suburbs, and corrugated-iron or tile roofs. Thatched mud-brick rondavels, once universal, survive only at the edges and in tourist lodges; modern South African-style malls and glass-fronted offices have arrived since 2009.
style.ornament: Basotho conical straw-hat (mokorotlo) silhouette on tourist and civic buildings, Basotho blanket stripe and diamond patterns in murals and railings, sandstone quoins and arched porches on colonial buildings, painted national-flag colours (blue, white, green, black) on signage and flagpoles.

sources.what: Maseru at ~1,600 m, subtropical highland climate, Kingsway first paved road, rondavels replaced by modern blocks, Cathedral of Our Lady of Victories and St John's as surviving colonial buildings, Pioneer/Maseru Mall era
